statusText: Tail holds at 20%. Mapped policy state: WATCH. The 31,196.75 session low has now held for about two hours and the 31,196.75-31,466.00 range is unchanged, so the 08:20Z bounce failed inside a consolidation rather than extending the decline. Brent at 104.22 on a second, weather-driven supply channel, a 5.72% 30-year and European banks at a three-month low keep Tail at the WATCH floor into the US cash open.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH with Tail at 20%, the floor of the 20-24% band and below the 25% blocking threshold. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 12:30Z-16:00Z, spanning the jobless-claims print, the US cash open and the first cash hours, where conditional Tail peaks at 22%. Conditional Tail sits at 19% in the EA_ON band from 10:00Z to 12:00Z and returns to that band from 16:00Z onward if intraday retracements of normal depth persist.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a two-hour base above the session low as the bounce fades, while crude above 104 on a second supply channel and a hawkish Waller keep conditions difficult
body:
The tenth Globex hour of the Oct 7-8 session has produced a base above the session low rather than a new leg down. NQ Dec26 traded 31,233.50 as of 09:16:25Z, -168.75 or -0.54% against a 31,402.25 prior close, corroborated at 31,246.00 on an independent feed around 09:15Z and at 31,231.25 and 31,226.50 on two further captures. The session range is unchanged from an hour ago at 31,196.75-31,466.00, worth 269.25 points or 0.86%: no new low and no new high. The 31,196.75 low set in the 07:00Z hour has now held for roughly two hours. The 08:20Z recovery to 31,276.50 has faded and price sits about 37 points above the low, so the bounce failed, but a failed bounce inside an unchanged range is consolidation, not the repeated extension after failed retracements that the risk contract treats as pathological. Today's low also remains above the 31,143.00 Oct 7 low, so the prior day's floor is intact. Tail therefore holds at 20%, the floor of the WATCH band, and the dominant mode stays mixed.

Tail does not ease into the EA_ON band because the backdrop broadened against equities within the hour, and a second supply channel for crude has now been verified. Brent trades 104.22, +4.02 or +4.01%, inside a 100.75-104.42 range, firmer than the 104.13 and +3.92% of an hour ago, with WTI Nov 26 around 91.86-91.94 and +4.1%. Alongside the continuing Hormuz attacks and the US-Iran conflict, Tropical Storm Isaias is approaching the US Gulf Coast with landfall expected Saturday and possible strengthening to hurricane force: Shell is evacuating and shutting in five platforms, Mars, Olympus, Ursa, Vito and Appomattox, and Chevron has shut in four, against offshore Gulf fields that supply roughly 15% of US oil output. The long end continues to rise, with the 10-year at 5.337%, up about 4.2 basis points and close to the 5.36% 24-year high set Oct 7, the 30-year at 5.72% and the 2-year at 4.81%. Europe is weaker in the same direction: as of 0833Z the STOXX 600 was -0.8% at 625.44, European banks were down nearly 2% at a more-than-three-month low, the CAC 40 was -1% at a six-month low, and euro-area yields reached multi-decade highs in a broad global bond selloff.

The 08:30Z Waller event, unresolved at the previous assessment, has now printed and is hawkish but not disorderly. In prepared remarks for the Central Bank of Turkey forum he said he anticipates additional hikes to support a timelier return of inflation to the 2% goal, while adding that the hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings, which leaves a pause at the Oct 27-28 meeting open. He cited a strengthening economy, the unresolved energy price shock tied to the Iran war and AI-buildout demand, and said he is not greatly concerned that tighter policy causes a damaging slowdown. The policy rate is 3.75-4% after a September quarter-point hike, and pricing still points to a hold in October and a hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting. Under the standing contract hawkish guidance, event importance and energy-driven inflation risk are Stress and Confidence inputs until observed NQ structure establishes mean-reversion failure, so Stress rises to 60% while Tail is unchanged.

The counterweights keep this a WATCH at the band floor. A 0.54% decline inside a 0.86% range that has not expanded in two hours is an orderly grind. VIX is 15.63 as of 09:11Z, +0.55 or +3.65% from a 15.08 close, which registers the risk-off tone without a volatility regime shift. Cash NDX closed Oct 7 at 31,160.08, -0.21%, after a 30,904.46 low that was fully retraced into the close, the standing precedent that mean reversion still functions in this regime. The 12:30Z claims print and the 13:30Z cash open are the next genuine structural checkpoints and have not occurred; the published danger window covers 12:30Z-16:00Z, where conditional Tail peaks at 22%. Confidence is 88%: quadruple-sourced NQ quotes through 09:16Z, live VIX and Brent, Oct 8 readings for the 2-, 10- and 30-year, verified Waller content closing the previous hour's main gap, a dual-sourced European cash wrap at 0833Z and a re-verified seven-day calendar support it. The gaps are an H.15 fix only through Oct 6, a 10-year discrepancy between a 5.28% ticker capture and the 5.337% Oct 8 reading, and no tick beyond 09:16Z. The shared Finviz evidence file was collected 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with partial status, about nine days past the 90-minute freshness contract, so it was excluded and this assessment rests entirely on independent research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 12-14% through the Oct 7 European hours, rose into a 20-23% WATCH band between 11:00Z and 15:00Z as a trend-down phase developed into the US cash open, then decayed steadily once the cash dip to 30,904.46 was fully retraced into the close. Every hour from 16:00Z through 05:00Z held the 10-18% EA_ON band with Stress at 47-53%. The final three lookback hours mark the current episode: Tail lifted to 14% at 06:00Z as the 05:16Z retracement failed, to 22% at 07:00Z after a second failed retracement set the 31,196.75 low, then eased to 20% at 08:00Z once that low held and the repeated-extension amplifier lapsed. Stress rose monotonically from 47% to 59% across the same stretch as crude and the long end climbed.
outlookSummary: Base case is that the two-hour base above 31,196.75 resolves into two-way rotation through European and US cash trade, while Brent above 104 on both Hormuz attacks and Gulf of Mexico storm shut-ins, a 10-year near its 24-year high, multi-decade-high euro-area yields and a confirmed Fed hiking bias remain the dominant background conflict. Conditional Tail eases to 19% in the EA_ON band from 10:00Z through 12:00Z, then rises across the 12:30Z claims print to a 22% peak spanning the 13:30Z cash open and the first full cash hour, which is the published 12:30Z-16:00Z danger window. It returns to the EA_ON band from 16:00Z and settles at 14-17% through the 30-year auction, the cash close and the overnight Globex and Asian hours, lifting marginally at the Tokyo and European opens. A break of 31,196.75 on expanding range with shallow pullbacks is the condition that would invalidate the decay path and argue for the blocking band.
